newsitem.title: SPAIN: OECD sees Spain meeting 2000 deficit target.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees Spain meeting 2000 deficit target.

text.p: Spain looks set to meet its deficit reduction target for 2000 and a sharp moderation in inflation should permit a relaxation in monetary policy, the OECD said on Thursday.

In its twice yearly report, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development said recent structural reform should help the government reach its target of lowering the government deficit to 1.6 percent of gross domestic product in 2000. The OECD said it expected Spain to have a deficit of 2.8 percent of GDP this year, the reference value for meeting the deficit criteria of the single currency.

"The structural reforms should lower structural unemployment and facilitate a further decline in the general government deficit over the medium-term, which is targeted in the government's new convergence programme to fall to 1.6 percent GDP in 2000," the report said.
In addition, a sharp drop in inflation means that monetary policy remains tight, despite a reduction in the key money market rate to 5.25 percent in May.
Consumer inflation moderation to 1.7 percent in April, while the pace of moderation accelerated this year.
"Monetary policy remains tight, as real short-term interest rates exceed three percent and capital inflows have until quite recently put upward pressure on the peseta.
"Thus, a further cautious relaxation of monetary policy may be expected following the consolidation of the recent inflation gains," the OECD said.
The OECD also said it expected growth to pick-up to three percent in 1998 from near three percent this year.
"Recent developments point to a broad-based strengthening of activity, which should push output growth to 3 percent by 1998," th OECD said.

NOTE - The table reflects percentage changes (1986 prices) except unemployment, which is a percentage of workforce, and household savings, which is a percentage of disposable income. General government financial balance and current account are percentages of GDP.
